items.title: Sun Life introduces a unified global brand identity under the name Sunlife
items.grounded_note: Sun Life Financial unveiled a refreshed global brand that brings its name together as “Sunlife,” introduces a modernized digital-oriented logo and adopts the tagline “Making life brighter.” The company said the unified identity reflects its expansion across insurance, health, wealth and asset management and is intended to create a more consistent expression across its worldwide operations. The underlying corporate purpose and client commitments were stated to remain unchanged.

items.title: Sun Life global survey identifies demand for integrated health, financial and protection support
items.grounded_note: Sun Life published research covering adults in eight North American and Asian markets, including Hong Kong, the Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore. Sixty-five percent of respondents wanted support that treats health, finances and protection as connected, while only 33% reported having a full plan for unexpected illness or accident costs and 31% had a full plan for family security. The study also found that 61% viewed health as affecting their financial position and 59% viewed finances as affecting health.

items.title: Hong Kong Insurance Authority disciplines six intermediaries for AML/CFT control breaches
items.grounded_note: The Hong Kong Insurance Authority banned or suspended six individuals from acting as insurance intermediaries for periods ranging from six to 13 months. The authority found that the individuals breached appointing insurers’ internal controls by helping customers falsely declare that they had purchased bank drafts, involving approximately HK$7.3 million in premium payments, while purchasing the drafts on the customers’ behalf. The action concerned named individuals and reinforced the requirement for intermediaries to comply with insurers’ anti-money-laundering and counter-financing-of-terrorism controls.

items.title: FSB consults on high-level principles for regulatory and supervisory modernisation
items.grounded_note: The FSB proposed eight high-level principles intended to help financial authorities make regulatory and supervisory frameworks more effective, efficient, risk-focused, coherent and forward-looking. The principles call for frameworks to respond to new vulnerabilities, technologies, financial offerings and economic conditions while preserving or enhancing financial-system resilience and remaining consistent with each jurisdiction’s laws and circumstances. The consultation applies across financial sectors, including insurance supervision in FSB jurisdictions; comments are due by 8 January 2027, with a final report planned for the first half of 2027.

items.title: Manulife launches proprietary enterprise AI platform across global operations
items.grounded_note: Manulife launched a proprietary enterprise AI platform providing a common operating environment for teams to build, deploy and manage AI solutions across its markets and jurisdictions. The platform embeds reusable components and security, risk and governance controls so previously approved use cases can be deployed more rapidly. Manulife said enterprise AI had generated US$300 million in value by year-end 2025 and is expected to produce US$1 billion in cumulative value by 2027 through expense reductions, revenue uplift, fraud reduction and growth absorption.

items.title: FWD to acquire 25% of bolttech Insurance Hong Kong and re-enter general insurance
items.grounded_note: FWD Group agreed to acquire a 25% stake in bolttech Insurance (Hong Kong) for a base consideration of US$20.72 million. The transaction would return FWD to Hong Kong’s property-and-casualty market after it divested the business, formerly FWD General Insurance, to bolttech in 2020. The investment represents a strategic expansion beyond FWD’s core life-insurance operations in Hong Kong.

items.title: AXA Future Risks Report ranks AI and big-data risks first among experts
items.grounded_note: AXA published its 13th Future Risks Report with Ipsos, reporting that artificial-intelligence and big-data risks ranked first among surveyed experts for the first time, rising from fourth place in 2025 and overtaking climate change. Among experts who placed AI among their leading risks, 54% viewed it as rapidly emerging while 9% believed public authorities were well prepared. The report also linked ageing, lower birth rates, longevity and changing family structures to evolving insurance needs in health, dependency protection, savings, retirement and wealth transfer.

items.title: Mainland China issues Property Insurance Company Insurance Product Development Management Provisions
items.grounded_note: The National Financial Regulatory Administration issued rules governing property insurers’ product-development organization, responsibilities and workflows. Property insurers must establish internal product-development management systems covering organizational structure, division of functions, processes, assessment and incentives; the rules also encourage products aligned with public protection needs and social development. The provisions take effect on November 1, 2026, replacing the 2016 product-development guidelines and a 2014 emergency notice on property-insurance product development and sales.

items.title: BNM confirms January 2027 MediAsas rollout and supporting Budget 2027 measures
items.grounded_note: Bank Negara Malaysia announced that MediAsas, a voluntary standardized medical and health insurance/takaful plan, will be rolled out publicly in January 2027. Premiums or contributions paid for the plan will qualify for income-tax relief when coverage is purchased for the taxpayer or immediate family members. Budget 2027 also allocates RM40 million for MediAsas vouchers for employees of SMEs with fewer than 75 employees, targeting workers who may have limited or no medical and health insurance/takaful coverage.

items.title: Taiwan exempts wealth-management life products from minimum death-benefit ratios
items.publisher: Financial Supervisory Commission, Taiwan / Executive Yuan Gazette
items.grounded_note: The Financial Supervisory Commission amended the minimum ratio rules for life-insurance death benefits relative to policy-value reserves or policy-account values, effective immediately. Life products sold to an insurer’s wealth-management clients are now exempt from the age-based minimum ratios, extending an approach previously tested in the Kaohsiung asset-management pilot area. Products outside an exemption remain subject to minimum ratios ranging from 190% for insured persons aged 30 or below to 100% for those aged 91 or above.

items.title: Citi forecasts a third-quarter decline in AIA value of new business amid regulatory and base-effect pressures
items.grounded_note: Citi forecast that AIA’s third-quarter value of new business would decline by 2.6% year on year at constant exchange rates and by 2% at actual exchange rates, ahead of operating data expected on October 30. The forecast cited a high comparison base and disruption to mainland China bancassurance business from regulatory changes; it also identified slower Hong Kong growth and tighter controls on mainland outbound investment as pressures on business linked to mainland visitors. Citi expected the base effect to normalize in the fourth quarter and retained a positive medium-term view.

items.title: MAS issues Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence Risk Management for Financial Institutions
items.grounded_note: MAS issued supervisory guidelines covering all forms of artificial intelligence used by financial institutions, including life, general, composite and captive insurers and insurance brokers. The guidelines require institutions to manage AI-related risks using approaches proportionate to their risk profiles and the scale and nature of their AI use. They were published on 7 October 2026 and will take effect on 7 October 2027.

items.title: Taiwan strengthens supervisory follow-up for firms with persistently weak fair-treatment assessments
items.grounded_note: Taiwan’s Financial Supervisory Commission completed its 2026 fair-treatment assessment of financial institutions, including 20 life insurers and 19 property insurers. The 130-point methodology assigns 100 points to implementation of ten fair-treatment principles and consumer-dispute outcomes, and 30 points to board-level leadership, with inspection and ongoing-supervision findings used as an additional deduction. Beginning with the 2026 assessment, firms placed in the bottom 20% for a second consecutive year must submit improvement plans and attend regulator-led special guidance meetings; AIA’s Taiwan branch was separately identified as the life insurer receiving the best-improvement distinction.

items.title: Taiwan proposes changes permitting insurers to maintain investment ratios after venture-investment businesses become publicly issued companies
items.grounded_note: Taiwan’s Financial Supervisory Commission proposed amendments to the rules governing insurers’ special-use investments in public and social-welfare enterprises. The draft deletes the obsolete category of “emerging important strategic enterprises” and would allow an insurer whose investment subsequently falls under specified Insurance Act investment categories to participate in capital increases at its original investment ratio even where that ratio exceeds the otherwise applicable statutory limits. The proposal was released for public comment under Taiwan’s administrative rulemaking process.

items.title: Taiwan expands the health and welfare businesses open to insurance-company investment
items.grounded_note: Taiwan’s Financial Supervisory Commission said it would issue an interpretation permitting insurers to invest in a broader range of health-promotion, long-term-care and related service businesses. Eligible activities include health-management and nutrition services, pharmacies, medical-data and digital-health platforms, software and connected devices, long-term-care support, accessibility services, specialized food and integrated service or distribution platforms. The interpretation also removes the previous requirement that each qualifying business have a direct connection with policyholders, insurance products, claims or insurance benefits, with classification instead based on its actual operations.

items.title: Taiwan amends insurers’ financial-reporting rules for IFRS 18 implementation
items.publisher: Financial Supervisory Commission, Taiwan / Executive Yuan Gazette
items.grounded_note: Taiwan’s Financial Supervisory Commission amended parts of the Regulations Governing the Preparation of Financial Reports by Insurance Enterprises and multiple prescribed reporting formats. The amendments incorporate IFRS 18 concepts, including revised requirements for aggregation and disaggregation, materiality assessments, comparative reporting and the presentation or disclosure of financial-statement line items. Article 37 applies from fiscal year 2027, while Articles 4, 9, 12, 15 and 29 and the amended formats under Articles 19, 22 and 23 apply from fiscal year 2028.

items.title: AIA shares hit a 52-week low amid higher US bond yields and concerns over Hong Kong and mainland China business momentum
items.grounded_note: AIA’s Hong Kong-listed shares fell as low as HK$68.05 on October 5, 2026, marking a 52-week low and a decline of about 26% from the year’s reported high of HK$92.15. The report linked the market pressure to rising long-term US Treasury yields, which can increase discount rates and affect investors’ valuation of insurers’ future cash flows and embedded value. It also cited concerns about slowing Hong Kong growth and tighter mainland outbound-investment controls potentially affecting new business associated with mainland Chinese visitors, while noting that AIA’s first-half annualised new premiums had risen 14.4% and its value-of-new-business margin was 57.1%.

items.title: MAS consults on targeted corporate-governance changes for banks, insurers and designated financial holding companies
items.grounded_note: MAS proposed amendments addressing director independence, board and board-committee composition, and regulatory approval of key appointments at banks, insurers and designated financial holding companies. Proposed measures include treating certain directors employed by or dealing with related corporations or affiliates as non-independent, increasing minimum board size and requiring majority-independent boards for domestic systemically important insurers, and extending prior-approval requirements to additional appointments. Consultation P016-2026 remains open until 11:59 p.m. on 9 December 2026.

items.title: BNM proposes revised proper-advice requirements for insurance and takaful sales
items.grounded_note: Bank Negara Malaysia issued an exposure draft setting proposed requirements and guidance for financial service providers and intermediaries that advise on, recommend or sell insurance and takaful products. The proposed framework covers governance and internal controls, customer suitability and affordability assessments, customer fact-finding, product recommendations, investment-linked product sales controls, sales-quality reviews and telemarketing controls. The draft would therefore affect both firms’ distribution governance and customer-facing sales processes across Malaysia’s insurance and takaful sector.

items.title: Sun Life Financial Resilience Index reports weakening household buffers across six Asian markets
items.grounded_note: Sun Life's 2026 Financial Resilience Index covered Hong Kong, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Vietnam. It reported that the proportion of highly financially resilient respondents declined from 32% in 2025 to 25% in 2026, while only 13% felt fully secure about their financial position. More than eight in ten said inflation had made monthly expenses harder to cover, one quarter were drawing down savings, and only 39% could support themselves for more than six months following job loss or illness.

items.title: Manulife Asia Care Survey examines extended dependency and retirement preparedness across nine Asian markets
items.grounded_note: Manulife's 2026 Asia Care Survey collected responses from more than 9,000 adults across the Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan, Singapore, Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines and Malaysia during February and March 2026. The research estimated that older adults in Asia may require care or financial support for 13 to 14 years and found that 82% viewed independence as the most meaningful legacy for their families. It also identified preventive-care gaps: only about half received a comprehensive health check at least annually, while around one in ten had never undergone one.

items.title: FSB identifies AXA Group among insurers subject to resolution-planning standards
items.grounded_note: The FSB’s current public list records AXA Group as one of 17 insurers reported by national authorities as subject to resolution planning and resolvability-assessment requirements consistent with Key Attributes 8–11. The standards are intended to prepare firms and authorities to manage significant distress or failure, including through cross-border cooperation; inclusion does not itself designate an insurer as systemically important. The FSB states that its 2025 list contains 17 insurers, compared with 13 in the 2024 list.
